inputs.prompt: A creature designer's anatomy reference page for a video game boss called the sand shark, drawn in confident pencil with light washes of dusty brick red, pale sand yellow and grey on cream paper, like a page from a creature anatomy book, with small neat hand lettered labels. Top row, four accurate studies of real animals side by side, each with its label underneath: the cartilage jaw of a great white shark, a ring of jaw lined with rows of triangular teeth, labelled "shark jaw"; a sandfish skink, a small stocky lizard with a shovel shaped snout, glossy scales and short legs, diving head first into sand, labelled "sandfish skink"; a spiny dogfish, a small slim grey shark with white spots and one short sharp spine in front of each of its two dorsal fins, labelled "dogfish spines"; a thresher shark with its very long curved tail, labelled "thresher tail". Middle of the page, large: the sand shark seen from the side, drawn as a skeleton study inside the faint outline of its body. Its body is long, low and flat, much lower than a normal shark's. Its head is a flat wedge like a shovel for cutting through sand. Its jaw is oversized, a third of its body length, packed with rows of teeth. Its skeleton is grey cartilage like a real shark's, with no ribs: a long backbone, the jaw, the fin supports and the tail. Along the backbone grows a row of long hollow spines that sweep backward and stick up out of its back. A tall blade shaped dorsal fin, and a heavy tail with a sickle shaped fin. Its back is washed dusty brick red, darker than the sand, and its belly is pale. Short labels with arrows: "jaw" pointing at the jaw, "fin" pointing at the dorsal fin, "spine rack" pointing at the row of spines, "tail" pointing at the tail. Along the bottom edge of the page, a thin strip: the same shark from the side swimming under the sand, drawn as a wavy sand line with only its dorsal fin and its row of spines sticking up above it and the faint shape of its body below the line, labelled "under the sand". Clean, technical, believable anatomy, no scenery, no other text.
